items.evidence: "ID presented research on standard components, noting that while push buttons are inexpensive, a wheel sensor is significantly more costly—approximately 50 times the price of a button." Voice recognition chip is covered: "Speaker 2 suggests exploring existing voice recognition technology from the manufacturing division" (transcript confirms the UI Designer raised it during the ID presentation).
"Speaker 2 proposes a simplified UI based on existing remote designs by removing unnecessary buttons."
Simpler by removing extra buttons is stated ("simplified interface by removing unnecessary buttons and focusing on central controls"), but the more ergonomic aspect of the UI design is not mentioned.
"Speaker 4 presents market trends suggesting that products should have a fancy look, be innovative, and remain easy to use."
"Current fashion trends suggest utilizing \"spongy\" materials and organic fruit or vegetable shapes."
Section "Final Concept Decisions and Next Steps" lists the features decided.

Banana shape, spongy, lighted buttons, top-mounted wheel, standard batteries and chip-on-print are all stated, but the notes do not say the chip excludes speech recognition; instead they list the voice recognition chip as an unresolved question. Transcript: PM deferred the voice decision and it was never explicitly revisited, though ID said they know exactly which standard chip to use.

"Speaker 1 instructs the industrial designer and UI designer to collaborate on developing the prototype's look and feel." and "Future tasks involve evaluating if the new design meets all user requirements before the next meeting."
Outline: "Speaker 1 instructs the industrial designer and UI designer to collaborate on developing the prototype's look and feel." (Action Items section itself says none.)
"Future tasks involve evaluating if the new design meets all user requirements before the next meeting."
"Decisions were made to include lighted buttons and a top-mounted wheel..."; "The final concept combines a banana-shaped spongy casing..."
"ultimately deciding on a yellow banana shape"; "The exterior will feature a spongy material"
"Decisions were made to include lighted buttons" (though elsewhere wrongly says they activate on movement).
"Despite this, the team decided to move forward with a wheel control to provide a competitive advantage and enhance innovation."

Notes say the build uses "chip-on-print technology" but treat the voice recognition chip as an open question rather than eliminated. Transcript never explicitly drops voice in this meeting (PM deferred it; earlier meeting had ruled out voice), so notes are only partly aligned.

errors.claim: The remote will include backlit buttons that activate upon movement to assist in dark environments
errors.why_wrong: Motion-activated lighting was only floated; the UI Designer objected that it needs an extra sensor and is too expensive, and the ID also mentioned continuous light. No decision on movement activation was made.

errors.claim: The final concept combines a banana-shaped spongy casing with an arched internal structure for component mounting.
errors.why_wrong: No one described an arched internal structure; the PM said an odd-shaped structure with a spongy cover.
